mission.display_title: Choose summaries and plots for a stated aim
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to turn yesterday's purpose map into exploratory craft (choosing summary statistics and visualisations that serve a named aim inside the exploratory stage)
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will refuse chart-surfing: the candidate must name the aim first, then justify one summary and one visualisation for that aim, before reading deep. So EDA becomes judgement, not decoration.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from 'EDA means looking at data' to 'I select summaries and visualisations that match variable type and analysis aim, and I can defend that choice closed-book.'
mission.learning_objective: Select and justify appropriate summary statistics and exploratory visualisations for a stated analysis aim and variable type.
mission.concept_focus: Variable type → suitable summary → suitable visualisation → aim alignment.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you built the purpose map for data analysis (1.1) (aims, stages, sources, reproducibility). Today you work inside the exploratory stage: summaries and visualisations chosen for a stated aim.
mission.why_now: 1.2.1 is the next lawful LO after purpose; examiners ask which summary or plot is appropriate; without aim-linked tool choice, correlation work tomorrow has nothing trustworthy to associate.
mission.expected_benefit: One defended summary-and-plot pair for a named aim. Study Progress for today's Session, not completion of all of 1.2.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Alpha Day 2 because Day 1 established aim and stage; the skill gap now is exploratory tool judgement under LO 1.2.1.
success_criteria: Closed-book, for a named variable type and aim, state one suitable summary statistic and why it fits.
Name one suitable exploratory visualisation for the same case and what pattern it is meant to reveal.
State one misuse (wrong summary or plot for the aim/type) you will refuse.
task_descriptions: Write Aim / Variable type / Summary / Plot as four linked boxes before opening the CMP.
Complete Guided Reading through CMP treatment of summary statistics and exploratory visualisations (1.2.1 centre).
Closed-book: defend one summary-and-plot pair and name one misuse.

session.session_educational_purpose: This Session exists to execute today's Mission: build and stress-test closed-book judgement on summaries and visualisations under a stated aim. Not to catalogue every plot type in the CMP.
session.session_tutor_purpose: In this hour I will set focus questions that force aim-first tool choice, exit for CMP work on 1.2.1, then retrieve a defended summary-and-plot pair. So exploratory craft is tested, not page count.
session.wrap_up: Session complete for Choose summaries and plots for a stated aim. You practised selective CMP reading on Syllabus 1.2.1 and stress-tested aim-linked summary and visualisation choice. This is Study Progress for today's block. Not Topic Complete for all of 1.2, and not yet association measures (tomorrow).
session.confidence_prompt: How confident are you that you could defend one summary-and-plot pair for a stated aim closed-book tomorrow morning? Rate 1–5 and give one honest warrant.

reading_guidance.lead_line: Purpose of this reading: use the CMP to learn how to choose summary statistics and exploratory visualisations for a stated aim and variable type. So exploratory work stays aim-led. Extract that method from the CMP, then stop after the 1.2.1 summaries-and-visualisations block.
focus_questions: Which summaries does the CMP pair with which variable types, and what aim does each summary serve?
Which exploratory visualisations are recommended, and what pattern is each meant to reveal?
Where does the CMP warn about a misleading summary or plot choice?
You will later defend, closed-book, one summary-and-plot pair for a stated aim and name one misuse.
misconception_watch: Watch for choosing plots because they look impressive rather than because they match the aim.
Watch for using the mean as a default summary when the distribution shape argues otherwise.
Watch for treating visualisation as optional decoration after 'the real maths.'

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: aim-linked summary
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Suppose your aim is descriptive and your variable is a right-skewed claim size. Which summary statistic would you lead with, and why is it preferable to a naive mean-only report?
knowledge_checks.body: Justify from distribution shape and aim. Not from software defaults.
hints: Skewed positive data often needs median/IQR or careful mean-with-shape warning.
Say what the mean alone hides.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Descriptive EDA on skewed claim sizes should not hide behind a lone mean; shape-aware summaries protect the aim.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Lead with median (and IQR or percentiles); the mean is pulled by the long right tail and can mislead a descriptive brief about typical claim size.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Defaulting to the mean because 'that is what we always compute.'
success_criteria: Clear reason tied to skew / atypical mean.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: visualisation and misuse
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For the same skewed claim-size case: (1) Name one exploratory visualisation you would use and what pattern it should reveal. (2) Name one visualisation or summary misuse you would refuse for this aim.
knowledge_checks.body: Pair a plot with a pattern, then refuse a misuse.
hints: Histogram, density, or boxplot are common exploratory choices for numeric skew.
Misuses: pie charts for continuous magnitude; mean-only dashboard; truncated axes that hide the tail.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Exploratory visualisations exist to reveal shape and extremes; refusing decorative or misleading displays is part of professional EDA.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Use a histogram or boxplot to reveal right skew and extreme claims. Refuse a pie chart (or a mean-only table) that hides the tail.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Naming a plot without saying what pattern it reveals.
success_criteria: Suitable plot named with pattern purpose.
